title: Bluesky Social App
description: Build a local-first social-feed learning app with publishing, topic filtering, profile views, likes, bookmarks, and resilient persistence.
problem: Learners need a source-grounded way to understand and extend Bluesky Social App while separating implemented behavior from demo data, simulations, and missing integrations.
audience: Third-year undergraduate students who have completed introductory programming and want a practical mobile mini-project.
prerequisites: Git basics and ability to run the platform tooling described in the source README
learning_outcomes: Explain and trace post records, seed fixtures, and pure feed operations in its named source files.
Explain and trace composer validation, length limits, and immutable insertion in its named source files.
Explain and trace likemap, bookmarkmap, toggles, and the saved-post projection in its named source files.
Explain and trace context state lifecycle, storage adapter, migration defaults, and corrupt data in its named source files.
Explain and trace tab selection, screen composition, action props, and theme tokens in its named source files.
Explain and trace node test coverage, pure-model boundaries, and absent protocol integration in its named source files.
Explain and trace end-to-end feature tracing, persistence evidence, and safe demo scope in its named source files.
Distinguish unit-test evidence from device, service, and deployment evidence.
Propose a safe, bounded extension without describing it as already implemented.
